## Setup

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(simr)
set.seed(12345)
```

The goal of this file is to conduct a power analysis to determine the smallest effect of repetition that can be determined with 80% power and 607 participants.

## Load data

```{r}
df <- subset(read.csv("repetition_texting_tm_data.csv", fileEncoding="UTF-8-BOM"), rating_type == "Eth")
```


## Power analysis

Defining original model with 607 subjects

```{r}
df_607 <- subset(df, subjId %in% 1:607) # select first 607 participants


m1 <- lmer(rating ~ exposure + (1|subjId) + (1|claim), data = df_607)
summary(m1)
```

Simulation to determine power as a function of effect size

Note: long output, can skip to "Simulation output" section for results

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, cache = TRUE}
#simulation parameters
range <- seq(-1,-1.5,-.1)
nsim <- 1000

#intializing variables
power <- c()

for (effectsize in range) {
  fixef(m1)["exposure"] <- effectsize
  
  psim <- powerSim(m1, test = fixed("exposure", "t"), nsim = nsim, alpha = .05)
  
  power <- c(power,psim$x/nsim)
}
```

## Simulation output

```{r}
plot(range, power*100, xlab = "Effect size (b)", ylab = "Power (%)", ylim = c(0,100))
abline(h= 80)


data.frame(range,power*100)
```

save.image(file='posthoc_power.RData')
